_note: Commodore 64 Phantasie I art (v1.4; the p1-c64 import, P1C64Art; reverse-engineering/c64/phantasie1/GRAPHICS.md). Monsters are the MX n sprite bands (one figure: the band's first sprites, expanded as the VIC does); portraits the HSPRIT pair of each race (none for UNDEAD); the title PIC.* (multicolour bitmap, doubled pixels); town.backdrop the town screen's six buildings at their places (FONT+HER's town characters); the map from FONT's characters as UTIL-3.O's routine prints them. Colours: Colodore (VICE colodore.vpl). Text: the remaster 5x7 font (the C64's sets are in font/). The item / feature pictures (items/) in the programs' colours, beside the find / trap / stairs / lock / exit texts (event.*, find_pictures; DOOR not shown). s221: the ending (P.END's Zeus from ZALL, the members' cloud, the lightning hand; ending_scene) and the party wipe (CEMETARY's temple, ghost and face; defeat_pictures, DOS's pages, defeat.figure.* = the HSPRIT idle figures in yellow, no UNDEAD figure) in ending/ and defeat/.
name: Commodore 64
_tile_maps: UTIL-3.O $C5C3 (SYS 49152 + 63): map byte b >= 120 prints a blank in black (fog); else class b / 10 prints PETSCII $C695[class] OR (text column AND 1) in colour $C688[class], one 8 x 8 character a cell, the region's 26 x 20 cells whole (text columns 1-26, rows 5-24): tile b is the even map column's character, b + 256 the odd one's. Bytes 40, 41 and 50-59 also place a yellow sprite (town 93, inn 94, dungeon 95) 4 pixels left of the cell (overlays, drawn at their size); the party is white sprite 92 the same way. The Client's map box holds 19 x 18 of the cells around the party (the C64 shows all 26 x 20). Dungeon: FONT characters $E6-$EC in grey (12) on black by DOS's cell ranges (as on screen, live s218); a cell not yet seen is the solid $20; the party is yellow sprite 91 over its cell.

title_sequence._note: B lines 200-420: the title picture (PIC.*) stays up while UTIL-3.O and the two fonts load (no key wait; its time is the disk's [?]), then the '1 - Start in Pelnor / 2 - Continue' text screen. Shown until a key, as the Apple packs do.

_find_pictures: s221 [C] (I's GRAPHICS.md 7, the compiled BASIC of OUTDOORS / DUNGEON, II's the same): a found item shows I$((IT - 1) / 20) (SHIELD ... GOOD TREASURE) in colour IC = 15, 7 if IX = 2 or IX >= 6, 14 if IX = 3, 3 if IX = 4; IX is a float, so the single-id colours hit ids 41, 61 and 81 only. find_pictures: [first id, last id, picture]. event.trap (light red 10, a spotted trap), event.stairs (grey 12), event.lock (brown 9, a locked door, kind 14, whatever the pick), event.exit (green 5, 8 x 6). DOOR is loaded by no program (no slot). The C64 prints them over the map; the Client draws each beside its text.
_portraits: portrait.{race}: HSPRIT blocks 2 race (idle) and 2 race + 1 (attacking), the pair the fight copies for a member of that race (live s218); yellow, the combat row's colour [~]. No UNDEAD pair.

ending_scene._note: s221 / s223 (GRAPHICS.md 9.1 / 9.4, P.END's compiled BASIC, ZALL's and UTIL-3.O's 6502): the C64's own steps in c64 (the remaster's ending screen fields below are its fallback and unused with c64). Positions are screen pixels (VIC x - 24, y - 50), colours Colodore indices. After the grant the closing text page (s224: P.END's 9 lines from column 0, row 2, green, and its key prompt at column 7, row 24; until a key). The speech is Core's 7 lines on the C64's rows. s226: the sounds are sid_sounds (the wind, the thunder, the clicks; GRAPHICS.md 9.6).

c64._note: P.END: the astral line (TD = 2); a cloud per slot (all slots 0..PO), x 90 - 30 m for m < PL = INT(PO / 2 + 1.1), else 240 + 30 (m - PL) (VIC), rising from y 240 to 150 a pixel per TD = 0.05, MC1 yellow / red every 2 steps; TD = 2; Zeus wiped in from the bottom (ZALL $4CC0: 104 rows, 7 frames each); TD = 2; per slot the lightning hand, the thunder (TD 0.3 + 0.2 + FOR 1400), the figure (64 + P(168): the member's own idle figure; yellow if P(18) != 0 else light grey), TD = 0.3, the hand off, TD = 0.7; 'Zeus smiles and says' (row 24) with the face cycling $C6-$CD (UTIL-3.O $C86E, 10 frames each), TD = 3; the speech on rows 18-24, a character at a time, each space 16 + RND * 8 jiffies, each line's end two RND * 8; the grant hand cycling $C0-$C5, TD = 12. vbl_hz: VICE's PAL [~] (an NTSC C64 runs the wipe and the animator at 60). The interpreter's own time (cloud_step_overhead, letter_seconds, the FOR 1400 in thunder_seconds) measured in VICE (PAL) [~].

defeat_pictures._note: s221 (GRAPHICS.md 9.2, CEMETARY live in VICE): DOS's pages (P1DosDefeatScene) with CEMETARY's pictures: defeat.temple (FONTO's temple, dark grey, doorway open), defeat.demon (the same with the Great Demon's face, purple), defeat.ghost (SKEL2's ghost, white), defeat.figure.<race> (CSPRIT = HSPRIT's idle figures, yellow: the RESURRECTED colour). The C64 colours each fate's figure (UNDEAD cyan, DESTROYED dark grey) where DOS clears a destroyed slot and draws race 15 for UNDEAD (no C64 picture: fallback) [~]; its door rises out of the doorway (not modelled) [~]. Row: ghosts at VIC y 170 (screen 120) at x 110 - 17.5 n + 35 k; here DOS's gap rule [~]. Lines: text row 23, blue (the C64's astral / demon lines; its fate lines take the fate's colour) [~].

c64_defeat._note: s223 (I's GRAPHICS.md 9.2 / 9.4, CEMETARY's compiled BASIC): runs by itself, no key. 'Your party has been defeated' (red, column 6, row 23), TL = 2; the temple (dark grey) with its door (sprite 7, light grey, x- and y-expanded, behind the characters) and the astral line (blue, column 1, row 23); a ghost per member at VIC y 170, x = INT((220 - 35 PO) / 2) + 35 k, one each TL = 0.3; a sound, TL = 2; the door rises from VIC y 77 to 0, one pixel each TL = 0.1; the face (purple, expanded, in front) and the demon's line, TL = 4; per member the rows cleared (an UNDEAD fate's name on row 21, column 1, cyan: undead_name_row), a sound with TL = 1.08, its line in the fate's colour, its ghost's block overwritten with CSPRIT block P(145) (its own figure) a byte per BASIC pass, still white (64 passes, the 4.1 s copy; s224 morph), then coloured, a destroyed member's then switched off (ON DF GOSUB), TL = 2; TL = 6. The interpreter's time around the waits measured in VICE (PAL, s223) [~]: ghosts 0.33 s apart, the fate sound 1.17 s, the copy 4.1 s. The C64's own fate rule and texts are not used: Core's fates and lines (I's UNDEAD line holds the name too [~]).

sid_sounds._note: s226 (GRAPHICS.md 9.6) [C]: the end screens' sounds as their programs write the SID ($D400 + register), in order; times in seconds from the sound's start (BASIC's TI waits; the VICE-measured interpreter time for the FOR loops, PAL). Played on one 6581 model per screen (Client Sid6581). wind / wind_stop: ZALL $4D40 / $4E46 (P.END step 3 to after the wipe's TD = 2), the IRQ routine $4D73 once a jiffy (zall_wind). thunder: P.END 0xbb6 per strike (its clear loop pokes $D400 only). click / click_off: P.END 0xc43 per space and line end, the gate off after the caller's 16 or RND * 8 jiffies. rumble: CEMETARY 0x90e after the ghosts, its gate never turned off (it sounds until the first fate's clear). fate: CEMETARY 0x97b per member. cheer: WIN 0x749; the sweeps' pass is the measured 9.928 s less the FOR loops at WIN's 1.042 ms a pass [~].
